packs.title: 生活理财：从零花钱到预算
packs.subject: 生活理财
packs.description: 20 道原创生活理财题，学习预算、储蓄、消费者权益与消费判断。

questions.question: 小明每周有 RM20 零花钱，花 RM12 后还剩多少？
questions.explanation: RM20 减去 RM12，剩下 RM8。

questions.question: “预算”最主要的用途是什么？
questions.explanation: 预算帮助安排有限资金的用途。

questions.question: 你有 RM50，想买 RM35 的书和 RM20 的玩具，最合理的做法是？
options: 先按需要选择并核算总价
questions.explanation: 两件共 RM55，超出预算 RM5。

questions.question: 哪一种行为属于“储蓄”？
options: 把部分零花钱留作日后使用
questions.explanation: 储蓄是把当前资源保留给未来。

questions.question: “需要”和“想要”有什么区别？
options: 需要是基本必要，想要是额外愿望
questions.explanation: 区分必要支出和可选消费能改善预算。

questions.question: 商品标价 RM24，折扣 RM4，实付多少？
questions.explanation: 实付价格为原价减优惠额。

questions.question: 两家商店同款笔分别卖 RM3 和 RM5，哪家更便宜？
questions.explanation: 在质量和条件相同时，RM3 比 RM5 便宜。

questions.question: “收据”一般可以帮助你做什么？
options: 核对付款记录与购买凭证
questions.explanation: 收据是交易记录，退换货时也可能有用。

questions.question: 看到“限时五分钟立刻付款”的广告，你应该先怎样做？
options: 比较价格并确认是否真的需要
questions.explanation: 倒计时可能制造冲动消费压力。

questions.question: 什么是“利息”？
options: 借贷或存款可能涉及的资金使用成本或回报
questions.explanation: 利息通常按本金、利率和时间计算。

questions.question: 想存 RM60，每周存 RM10，大约需要几周？
为什么不应随意分享银行卡密码？
options: 可能让别人未经许可使用账户
questions.explanation: 银行卡密码属于敏感的金融验证信息。

questions.question: 现金付款和电子付款有什么共同点？
options: 都应该核对实际支付金额
questions.explanation: 无论支付方式，都需要确认金额与收款对象。

questions.question: 如果商品出现质量问题，最实用的第一步是什么？
options: 立即公开所有个人资料
保存凭证并联系合法销售渠道
questions.explanation: 保留证据有助于与商家沟通。

questions.question: “单价”可以帮助你比较什么？
questions.explanation: 单位价格可以比较每克或每件的成本。

questions.question: 同样的饮料，250 mL 售 RM2，500 mL 售 RM3，哪个每毫升更划算？
questions.explanation: 每毫升分别为 RM0.008 和 RM0.006。

questions.question: 什么是“紧急备用金”？
options: 留给意外必要支出的储蓄
questions.explanation: 备用金可以帮助应付突发的合理开支。

questions.question: 购买数字游戏道具前，为什么要先确认费用？
options: 所有付费道具都能退款
付款不需要监护人知道
虚拟购买也可能产生真实支出
questions.explanation: 游戏内购买也会消耗真实资金。

questions.question: 朋友向你推荐“稳赚不赔”的投资，哪种判断更审慎？
options: 邀请同学一起冲动投资
怀疑保证回报的说法并向可信成年人求证
questions.explanation: 任何投资都有风险，保证高回报的说法值得警惕。

questions.question: 每月记录自己的花费，最大的价值是什么？
options: 发现消费习惯并改进安排
questions.explanation: 记录支出能帮助识别不必要的花费。

packs.title: Young Entrepreneurs: Ideas & Customers
packs.subject: Entrepreneurship
packs.description: 20 realistic questions about business ideas, customer needs, feedback and simple costs.

questions.question: What is a business customer?
options: Someone who buys or uses a product or service
questions.explanation: Customers are people or organisations served by a business.

questions.question: A team wants to sell reusable bottles. What should it learn first?
options: How to copy every rival logo
Whether customers need and want the bottles
The colour of the founder's shoes
questions.explanation: Understanding customer needs helps define a useful product.

questions.question: What does a prototype help a team do?
options: Test an early version of an idea
questions.explanation: A prototype lets people try and evaluate a concept.

questions.question: What is revenue?
options: Money received from selling goods or services
Only the money left after expenses
questions.explanation: Revenue is sales income before subtracting expenses.

questions.question: What is a cost to a small bakery?
questions.explanation: Ingredients are resources the bakery pays for.

questions.question: A school stall sells ten bookmarks for RM3 each. What is total sales revenue?
questions.explanation: Ten multiplied by RM3 equals RM30 in revenue.

questions.question: If revenue is RM30 and total expenses are RM18, what is the simple profit?
questions.explanation: Profit is revenue minus expenses, here RM12.

questions.question: Why should a startup ask users for feedback?
options: To learn what actually works and what needs improvement
To prove its first idea is always perfect
questions.explanation: User feedback helps identify problems and improvements.

questions.question: What is a value proposition?
options: A list of all employee birthdays
A clear explanation of how a product helps customers
questions.explanation: A value proposition states the benefit a customer can expect.

questions.question: Which is an ethical way to promote a product?
questions.explanation: Accurate claims support customer trust.

questions.question: A competitor offers a similar product. What should a founder do?
options: Understand differences and improve their own offer
questions.explanation: Fair competition focuses on genuine customer value.

questions.question: What does a break-even point describe?
options: The level where revenue covers costs
A moment when no product can be sold
When a shop closes every day
questions.explanation: At break-even, total revenue equals total costs.

questions.question: Why does accessibility matter for a student app?
options: More people can use it despite different abilities
questions.explanation: Accessible design reduces unnecessary barriers.

questions.question: What is a recurring customer?
options: A customer who returns to buy or use a service again
questions.explanation: Returning users can indicate continuing usefulness.

questions.question: What should a team do with a failed prototype?
options: Identify the cause and revise the design
questions.explanation: Failure information supports iteration.

questions.question: What is a partnership in a project?
options: Two parties cooperating toward agreed goals
One person secretly using another's brand
questions.explanation: A partnership is cooperation based on an agreed purpose.

questions.question: Why track simple business metrics?
options: To make graphs look impressive only
To observe progress against a goal
questions.explanation: Useful metrics help identify changes over time.

questions.question: A customer reports a real problem. Which response is best?
options: Listen, investigate and communicate a resolution
questions.explanation: Respectful support and investigation can resolve issues.

questions.question: Why should product prices be transparent?
options: Only the seller should know the cost
Customers need to understand what they will pay
Prices have no effect on decisions
questions.explanation: Clear pricing supports informed choices.

questions.question: A business idea collects students' personal data. What should the team prioritize?
options: Collect only necessary data and protect it
Use the same password for all staff
questions.explanation: Privacy should be built into the product from the beginning.

packs.title: Media Detectives: Facts & Misinformation
packs.subject: Media Literacy
packs.description: 20 media literacy scenarios about sources, misleading posts, social networks and verification.

questions.question: A viral post has no named source. What is a sensible first step?
options: Edit it to sound more dramatic
questions.explanation: Popularity is not evidence that a claim is correct.

questions.question: What is a primary source for a speech?
options: A recording or transcript of the original speech
questions.explanation: Primary sources provide direct evidence.

questions.question: What is a headline's main purpose?
options: Introduce the subject and attract a reader
questions.explanation: A headline summarises or promotes content but cannot replace verification.

questions.question: A photo from 2019 is shared as today's flood. What is the problem?
options: The image is presented with misleading timing
questions.explanation: An authentic image can mislead when placed in false context.

questions.question: How can you check whether a photograph is reused elsewhere?
options: Ask the poster to use more emojis
Search for earlier appearances of the image
questions.explanation: Earlier appearances may reveal the photo's original context.

questions.question: What is an opinion?
options: A personal judgement that may differ between people
A measurement guaranteed to be exact
questions.explanation: Opinions express preferences or judgements.

questions.question: Which statement is directly verifiable?
options: The event begins at 9:00 AM on Saturday
This is the best event ever
questions.explanation: A published schedule can verify a stated starting time.

questions.question: A sponsored post promotes a product. What should viewers recognise?
options: No sponsorship disclosure is ever needed
The creator may have a commercial incentive
questions.explanation: Sponsorship can affect the motivation behind a message.

questions.question: What is confirmation bias?
options: Preferring information that supports existing beliefs
Changing the topic of a report
questions.explanation: People may selectively notice evidence supporting their views.

questions.question: Why compare reports from multiple independent sources?
options: It replaces direct observation in every case
It can reveal mistakes and missing context
It removes the need for evidence
questions.explanation: Independent reporting can improve confidence.

questions.question: What is a deepfake?
options: Synthetic media made to imitate a real person or event
questions.explanation: AI-generated video or audio can simulate appearances or voices.

questions.question: A convincing AI voice note asks for money. What is safest?
options: Assume the voice cannot be forged
Verify identity through a separate trusted channel
questions.explanation: Voice recordings can be imitated, so verification matters.

questions.question: What does a citation help readers do?
options: Locate the evidence supporting a claim
questions.explanation: Citations let others inspect the source material.

questions.question: Why can a cropped chart be misleading?
options: It may hide important axis values or comparison context
questions.explanation: Missing scales can exaggerate or minimise differences.

questions.question: An online claim cites 'experts' but no names or studies. What is missing?
options: Identifiable evidence that can be checked
questions.explanation: Unspecified authorities are difficult to verify.

questions.question: Which question is useful when reading a news article?
options: Can it make me angry quickly?
Does it have many capital letters?
Who produced it and what evidence supports it?
questions.explanation: Assessing source and evidence helps evaluate accuracy.

questions.question: What is clickbait?
options: A sensational heading designed to attract clicks
questions.explanation: Clickbait often prioritises clicks over clear context.

questions.question: Which is a responsible way to correct a mistaken post?
options: Explain the correction and provide reliable evidence
questions.explanation: Evidence-based corrections help others update beliefs.

questions.question: Why distinguish a simulation from real footage?
options: Viewers deserve to know what actually happened
All visual media must be forbidden
Reality can be determined by video quality alone
questions.explanation: Labels prevent fictional reconstructions from being mistaken for records.

questions.question: A study cited online has only ten participants. What should you consider?
options: That the conclusion must be universal
That every small study is fraudulent
Whether the sample size and design support the claim
questions.explanation: Study design and sample size affect how findings can be interpreted.

packs.title: Farms, Food Systems & Agriculture
packs.subject: Agriculture
packs.description: 20 questions on crops, soil, sustainable farming, pollination and food supply chains.

questions.question: Why do farmers rotate different crops across seasons?
options: To help maintain soil health and manage pests
To make every plant look identical
questions.explanation: Crop rotation can reduce some pests and improve nutrient balance.

questions.question: Which plant part usually develops into a fruit after fertilisation?
questions.explanation: In flowering plants, the ovary commonly develops into a fruit.

questions.question: What is compost?
options: A type of plastic fertiliser bottle
Decomposed organic material used to enrich soil
questions.explanation: Compost returns organic matter and nutrients to soil.

questions.question: Why are bees important to many crops?
options: They make every plant grow instantly
questions.explanation: Pollinators enable fertilisation for many flowering plants.

questions.question: Which practice helps conserve irrigation water?
questions.explanation: Drip systems can deliver water efficiently to roots.

questions.question: What does a seed need to germinate in most common crops?
questions.explanation: Seeds typically germinate when conditions are suitable.

questions.question: How do earthworms often help gardens?
options: They improve soil structure as they move and feed
questions.explanation: Earthworm activity can support soil aeration and nutrient cycling.

questions.question: What is a greenhouse used for?
questions.explanation: Greenhouses let growers adjust aspects of the environment.

questions.question: Why should farmers check soil moisture?
options: To choose the colour of baskets
To decide when plants need watering
To predict the next year's prices exactly
questions.explanation: Soil moisture can guide irrigation decisions.

questions.question: What is an invasive pest?
options: An organism that can harm crops outside its native balance
questions.explanation: Some introduced organisms cause damage when populations spread.

questions.question: Which crop is especially important as a staple food in Malaysia?
questions.explanation: Rice is a major staple food in Malaysia.

questions.question: What is a food supply chain?
options: The stages from growing food to delivering it to consumers
A metal chain around a field
questions.explanation: Supply chains involve production, processing, transport and sales.

questions.question: What can happen when harvested vegetables are stored too warm?
questions.explanation: Temperature control helps preserve freshness.

questions.question: What is hydroponics?
options: Growing plants with nutrient solutions without conventional soil
questions.explanation: Hydroponics supplies nutrients through water-based growing systems.

questions.question: Why might farmers use mulch around plants?
options: To remove all oxygen from the air
To reduce evaporation and suppress some weeds
questions.explanation: Mulch can protect soil moisture and moderate temperature.

questions.question: What is sustainable farming aiming to balance?
options: Food production with long-term environmental and resource care
Harvest size at any environmental cost
questions.explanation: Sustainable methods aim to protect resources while producing food.

questions.question: Why can monoculture create risk for farms?
options: A single crop may be vulnerable to the same pest or disease
It always produces ten crops at once
questions.explanation: Low crop diversity can increase shared vulnerability.

questions.question: What is a natural predator used for in pest management?
questions.explanation: Biological control can use predators of crop pests.

questions.question: Which food waste practice can help a household garden?
questions.explanation: Suitable biodegradable scraps can become compost.

questions.question: What is the purpose of farm-to-market transport?
options: Eliminate the need for packaging in every case
Deliver harvested food to buyers safely and efficiently
questions.explanation: Transport connects producers to processors, sellers and consumers.
